solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Quiet about desire to be like Kate

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
RE is Latin for 'concerning', a common crossword sense of about
a wish is a desire

explanation.surface: Someone keeps quiet about wanting to resemble a woman named Kate.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate is Katharina, the heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, so the reference points to the play rather than to any modern Kate.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Kate is the shrew of the play's title, so being like her means being bad-tempered and scolding.

clue.text: Rarely encountered blemish — Church providing support

indicators.note: in a down clue the church sits below, holding up the blemish

parts.note: a scar is a mark on the skin
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A rare flaw: the church comes to its aid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer CE comes underneath SCAR, so it is 'providing support'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, so it is seldom found or met with.

clue.text: Artist heads off sadly having left you in ill-considered way

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician

indicators.note: the heads, or first letters, come off the words that follow

explanation.surface: A painter goes off unhappily after leaving you, acting thoughtlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heads off' takes the first letters of 'sadly having left you', SHLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting hastily without thought is behaving recklessly or impetuously.

clue.text: It's part of law in term time

indicators.note: the answer forms a part of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Something is an element of the law during the legal term.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'laW IN TERm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Winter is a season, a period of the year, so a time.

clue.text: Ha! An ensign out to create mischief

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A naval officer laughs on going out to cause trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand tricks and high jinks amount to mischievous behaviour.

clue.text: Dislike French article about swearword

indicators.note: the article goes round the swearword, as about can mean surrounding

parts.note: le is the French masculine definite article
an oath can be a curse or swearword

explanation.surface: A French piece of writing objects to a rude word.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to hate intensely, a strong form of dislike, both used as verbs.

clue.text: Where cockney lives, character not finishing dish

parts.note: a cockney drops the H of home, saying 'ome

indicators.note: the word is left incomplete, its last letter taken away

parts.note: a letter of the alphabet is a character

explanation.surface: A Londoner's home and an unfinished letter make a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class East Londoner who drops initial Hs. 'not finishing' cuts the R from LETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a cooked egg preparation served as a meal or course.

clue.text: Cross note about partygoers

indicators.note: the note goes round the partygoers, about meaning around

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
ravers go to raves, wild parties

explanation.surface: An angry message about people out partying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry; it is the verb meaning to go across.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse land is to travel across it, the verb sense of cross.

clue.text: Permanent outcome, you heard, imposed on group

indicators.note: in a down answer the earlier pieces are placed on top of the group

parts.note: the end is the outcome or result

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the word said aloud is you, sounding like the letter U
a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A lasting result, you understand, is forced on a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns 'you' into the letter U; 'imposed on' places END and U above RING in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-lasting persists indefinitely, so it is effectively permanent.

clue.text: One missing president, tense, upset inwardly

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the president's name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: the letters of tense are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A single absent president is anxious and troubled inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Abe is the familiar name of Abraham Lincoln; 'tense' looks like a description of the president but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fails to turn up is a person missing from where they should be.

clue.text: Insistence of daughters to welcome celebrity rebuffed

indicators.note: the two D's take in the other piece as hosts welcome a guest

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a big name is a famous person

explanation.surface: Daughters insist on receiving a celebrity who has turned them down.
explanation.definitionFit: A demand is a forceful request, the noun sense of insistence on getting something.

clue.text: Learner, accused unfairly — one way out here?

indicators.note: unfairly treated letters are twisted out of their proper order

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A trainee wrongly charged looks for an escape.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a dead-end street has only one exit, the way you came in.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead-end street can only be left by the route used to enter, so it has a single exit.

clue.text: Measuring device on both sides of old Comet

indicators.note: the device's letters flank the abbreviation, lying either side of it

parts.note: a meter measures gas, electricity and so on

explanation.surface: A gauge placed around an ancient comet.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely, a shooting star or comet is a blazing body crossing the sky, the popular sense rather than the astronomer's.

clue.text: Confronting foe newly with fact — brought over expert

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is brought over, placed on top of, the expert
newly suggests the letters are made over afresh, rearranged

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Facing an enemy with a newly found fact after a specialist is flown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' rearranges FOE and FACT to FACETOF; 'brought over' sets it above ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting someone directly in person means being in confrontation or opposition.

clue.text: Versatile bar pianist having broad support

indicators.note: a versatile performer can turn into many forms, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An adaptable pub pianist is popular with everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Policy backed by both main parties enjoys wide support across the political divide.

clue.text: Line slimmer perhaps has adopted in the morning

indicators.note: the slimmer takes the time in, adopting it inside

parts.note: a slimmer is one example of a dieter
AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Someone trying to lose weight takes up a morning routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is a straight line through the centre of a circle.

clue.text: Spooner's cheerful admirer — he'll get you across the water

definitions.text: he'll get you across the water

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words change places

parts.note: merry means cheerful
a fan is an admirer

explanation.surface: A clergyman's happy devotee will take you over the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of MERRY FAN gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatman who carries passengers over a river or strait for a fare.

clue.text: More severe — cold leader suppressing the Spanish

parts.note: C is short for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the leader holds down the article, keeping it inside

parts.note: a ruler leads a country
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A chilly dictator crushes the Spaniards, getting harsher.
explanation.definitionFit: Crueller is the comparative of cruel, meaning harsher or more brutal.

clue.text: It helps to start conversation in ship

definitions.meaning: an opening remark or game that eases social awkwardness
a vessel built to cut through frozen seas

explanation.surface: A conversation opener aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a party opener that melts social frost and a vessel smashing polar ice clearing passage.

clue.text: Principal means of fastening papers

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, main or chief, as in a basic food
a bent wire clip driven through sheets to hold them together

explanation.surface: The chief method of binding documents together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a main or basic item, like a staple diet, and the little wire clip from an office stapler.

clue.text: Animal container, popular, English

parts.note: a can is a tin container
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A pet carrier that is fashionable in England.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, relating to dogs, and as a noun a dog itself, which is an animal.

clue.text: Respectable kind

definitions.meaning: conforming to accepted standards of behaviour
generous and obliging, as in 'that's very good of you'

explanation.surface: Someone worthy and generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both proper and morally upright, and also good-natured, obliging toward others.

clue.text: Place selling old currency gets stripped

parts.note: the mark was the German currency before the euro

indicators.note: stripped means the word loses its outer layer, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Somewhere a former currency is traded gets laid bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripped' takes the outside letters off GETS, leaving ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A market is where traders sell goods, so it is a place of selling.

clue.text: Again accepting that ultimately disclosure ban is needed for loan

indicators.note: the outer word takes in the other pieces, accepting them inside

parts.note: more can mean again, as in once more

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word that

parts.note: a gag order bans publication of information

explanation.surface: A legal gagging order is needed before a lender will advance money again.
explanation.walkthrough: A gag is a court order banning publication, hence 'disclosure ban'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is a loan secured on property, typically used to buy a house.

clue.text: One working for time at extremely large place of worship

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker, employed for a limited time

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of large

explanation.surface: A short-term worker at a huge church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives LE, the first and last letters of 'large'.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a building dedicated to religious worship, Hindu, Jewish or ancient.

clue.text: A Parish Priest in county setting — a jewel!

indicators.note: a setting holds a gem, so the county surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: shire is an old word for an English county

explanation.surface: A country parson set in rural county life is a real gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' works as a jeweller's setting, which holds a stone all round.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapphire is a precious blue gemstone, one kind of jewel.

clue.text: Have no more water — divers getting new start!

indicators.note: the opening letter is changed for a fresh one, giving the word a new beginning

parts.note: divers is an old adjective meaning various, sundry

explanation.surface: Underwater swimmers whose air supply fails need a fresh beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not swimmers but the archaic word for various; 'getting new start' swaps its first letter S for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A well or river that runs dry stops supplying, with its stock of liquid exhausted.

clue.text: Sherries served regularly at secluded place, tranquil in extreme

indicators.note: every other letter of the drinks is served up, at regular intervals

parts.note: a nest is a snug, hidden retreat

explanation.surface: Fortified wines handed round in a quiet hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served regularly' takes alternate letters of 'Sherries', SERE.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of calm and peaceful, describing the most untroubled state possible.
